units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Song of Songs 5:10">Targ. Cant. V, 10</cite>.

<cite ref="Megillah 18b:9">Meg. 18ᵇ</cite>, a. e. (expl. <he>מתנמנם</he>, v. <cite ref="N00669"><he>נִים</he></cite>) <he>דקרו … ולא ידע לאהדורי ס׳</he> you call him, and he answers but cannot recall an argument.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:4:8">Y. Ber. III, 6ᶜ</cite> top <he>כל סבר קשי דהוה לי תמן סבירתיה</he> any hard thinking I had to do, there I did it.
Ib. כל ההוא סברא קשיא וכ׳ all that difficult subject of T’bul Yom I studied there.—Esp. logical deduction, conclusion by reasoning, opp. to גמרא verbal tradition.
<cite ref="Yoma 33a:12">Yoma 33ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>גמרא גמירנא ס׳ לא ידענא</he> I know the final decision as a tradition, the argument I do not know.
<cite ref="Gittin 6b:10">Gitt. 6ᵇ</cite> <he>בשלמא מילתא דתליא בס׳ לחיי וכ׳</he> if it were a thing which depends on reason, you might be right, but this is a tradition.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 77a:1">B. Bath. 77ᵃ</cite> <he>גמרא או ס׳</he> is this a tradition or a logical inference? <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 34b:13">Ab. Zar. 34ᵇ</cite> <he>איבעית אימא ס׳ ואב״א קרא</he> I may say, it is founded on reason, or I may say, it is intimated in the Scriptures; a. v. fr.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:2:4">Y. Ber. IX, 13ᶜ</cite> bot.; <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 18:10">Midr. Till. to Ps. XVIII, 8</cite> <he>כך הוא ס׳ דמילתא</he>, v. <cite ref="O00089"><he>סֵבֶר</he></cite> 3.
